items.stem: Why can Nginx's event-driven model serve many concurrent connections efficiently?

options.text: It handles many connections per worker with asynchronous events instead of one thread each
options.rationale: Correct: an event loop multiplexes many connections per worker, avoiding per-connection thread overhead.

options.text: It opens a new operating-system process for every single request
options.rationale: That is the model Nginx avoids; it would not scale well.

options.text: It refuses connections beyond a small fixed number
options.rationale: The event model exists to handle large numbers, not to cap them low.

options.text: It serves only one client at a time

items.explanation: Correct: an event loop multiplexes many connections per worker, avoiding per-connection thread overhead.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid roles for Nginx in front of an application? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Terminating TLS and forwarding plain requests to the app
options.rationale: Correct: TLS termination at the proxy is a standard Nginx role.

options.text: Load-balancing requests across several upstream app servers
options.rationale: Correct: distributing traffic across upstreams is a core reverse-proxy role.
Nginx is a web server/proxy, not a database.
Nginx does not build application code.

items.explanation: Correct: TLS termination at the proxy is a standard Nginx role.

items.stem: Clients get intermittent 502 Bad Gateway responses from an Nginx reverse proxy. What is the best first diagnostic step?

options.text: Check the Nginx error log and the upstream server's health
options.rationale: Correct: a 502 means the upstream failed to respond properly; the error log and upstream status reveal why.
Deleting the config removes the proxy rather than diagnosing the fault.

options.text: Assume the client's browser is broken
options.rationale: A systemic 502 points at the proxy or upstream, not individual browsers.
Disabling logs removes the evidence needed to diagnose the error.

items.explanation: Correct: a 502 means the upstream failed to respond properly; the error log and upstream status reveal why.
